events.title: The Mayflower Departs Plymouth
events.description: The Mayflower set sail from Plymouth, England, carrying 102 passengers, including Pilgrims seeking religious freedom, bound for the New World. After a roughly 66-day voyage, it reached Cape Cod in November 1620.
events.significance: The voyage led to the founding of Plymouth Colony, one of the earliest permanent English settlements in New England, and became a foundational story in American history.

events.title: Grito de Dolores Begins the Mexican War of Independence
events.description: Catholic priest Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla called on the people of Dolores, Guanajuato, to rise up against Spanish colonial rule. His call to arms sparked a decade-long struggle for independence.
events.significance: The event is commemorated annually as Mexican Independence Day and marks the start of the movement that ended Spanish rule in Mexico in 1821.

events.title: Papua New Guinea Gains Independence
events.description: Papua New Guinea became an independent nation after decades of administration by Australia, with Michael Somare as its first prime minister. It remained a member of the Commonwealth.
events.significance: Independence marked the end of Australian colonial administration and established a new sovereign state of great cultural and linguistic diversity in the Pacific.

events.title: Montreal Protocol Signed
events.description: Representatives of many nations signed the Montreal Protocol on Substances That Deplete the Ozone Layer, committing to phase out the production of chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting chemicals.
events.significance: Widely regarded as one of the most successful international environmental agreements, it has helped the ozone layer begin to recover.

events.title: Death of Maria Callas
events.description: The American-born Greek soprano Maria Callas died in Paris at age 53. Renowned for her dramatic intensity and vocal range, she transformed 20th-century opera performance.
events.significance: Callas is regarded as one of the greatest opera singers of all time and helped revive interest in the bel canto repertoire.
